hints.content: Dropping by $5\%$ each year means the population keeps $100\%-5\%=95\%$ of its size each year.
So each year, the population size is multiplied by $95\%$, which is the same as a factor of $0.95$.

If we start with the initial value, $200$ lions, and keep multiplying by $0.95$, this function gives us the size of the population $t$ years from now:

$P(t)=200(0.95)^t$

question.content:
